title: Exact oxygen and two isotope ratios permit a 35 umol/kg oxygen spread in a two-component model with uncertain fractionation
abstract: We tested whether oxygen-17 and oxygen-18 ratios distinguish uniform oxygen use from mixing when respiratory fractionation is uncertain. We derived an exact map from the isotope moments of any closed-parcel mixture to the factors of an equal-oxygen uniform state. A constructed 50:50 mixture at 90 and 160 umol/kg has the same mean oxygen and both isotope ratios as a uniform state at 125 umol/kg. The mixture has an oxygen standard deviation of 35 umol/kg. The required fractionation factors lie within an illustrative envelope based on two laboratory cultures. A slope change of 0.000290 removes a 3.80 ppm oxygen-17 ratio mismatch after oxygen-18 is matched. We report 901 split tests, 49 calibration budgets, explicit positive witnesses and an independent high-precision audit. The result hides the distribution of oxygen use, not its mean under a known common source. It does not identify the cause of the California low or a ventilation share. Source uncertainty, environmental calibration, repeated mixing and reaction, and other isotopologues remain outside the test.
